sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: LLMs-from-scratch is the official code for Sebastian Raschka's book Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch). It walks you through coding, pretraining and fine-tuning a small GPT-like model in PyTorch, step by step.
sixtySeconds.problem: It's hard to understand how models like ChatGPT work by only using them. This repository builds one from the ground up, from text processing and attention to training and instruction fine-tuning, without external LLM libraries.
whoFor: Python developers who want to understand LLMs deeply
Engineers moving into AI who want hands-on practice
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want to learn by building, with notebooks per chapter. The code runs on ordinary laptops. The book itself is sold separately; the code is free.
requirements: Basic PyTorch helps (Appendix A introduces it)
A regular laptop is enough; a GPU is used automatically if available

overview: The repository follows the book chapter by chapter: working with text data, coding attention mechanisms, implementing a GPT model, pretraining on unlabeled data, fine-tuning for text classification and fine-tuning to follow instructions. Each chapter has Jupyter notebooks and summary scripts plus exercise solutions.

Appendices cover an introduction to PyTorch, extras for the training loop, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA. The method mirrors how large foundation models are built, scaled down for learning.

The main chapters are designed to run on conventional laptops in reasonable time. A setup folder explains how to install Python and packages, and there's a troubleshooting guide. A 17-hour companion video course and a sequel book on reasoning models are available separately.
